plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above broad blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from simple single blooms to ruffled parrot and double forms. Peak bloom occurs in the Netherlands and across northern temperate gardens in early May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, Northern Europe, North America; native to Central Asia, cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so valuable during Dutch 'Tulip Mania' that a single rare bulb could cost more than a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces dramatic hanging clusters of fragrant flowers, often 20-30 cm long, before or as its leaves emerge. It twines counterclockwise and can live for decades, covering pergolas and walls.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the eastern and western United States
plants.funFact: A Chinese wisteria in Sierra Madre, California, planted in 1894, is considered one of the largest blossoming plants in the world, covering about an acre and weighing hundreds of tons.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tropical and subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere the tree's main bloom is in spring (Oct-Nov), but in parts of the tropics and in warmer areas it also flowers in late autumn and sporadically at other times. In northern hemisphere subtropical regions such as parts of Mexico, Florida, and southern Asia, blooming peaks around May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; grown in Mexico City, Florida, southern California, India, and Pakistan
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, jacaranda blossoms carpet streets in spring, and the trees were introduced there by a Japanese gardener, Tatsugoro Matsumoto, in the early 20th century.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that forms dense, nodding carpets of fragrant, bell-shaped flowers beneath deciduous trees. The flowers droop to one side on arching stems and signal the height of spring in ancient British woodlands.
plants.location: Native to the British Isles, Western Europe, and Atlantic coastal regions; ancient woodlands in England, Wales, and Ireland
plants.funFact: Nearly half of the world's bluebells grow in Britain, and it is illegal to dig up wild bluebell bulbs for sale under the Wildlife and Countryside Act.
